original_options.label: C
original_options.text: Aging is the solution of the starvation problem in the case of priority scheduling.

original_options.label: D
original_options.text: Critical section is a resource that cannot be accessed by multiple processes concurrently.

question_revision.stem: Which statements are false? Interpret aging under a priority scheme and workload where increasing waiting jobs’ priority prevents indefinite postponement. Select all that apply.

options.label: A
options.text: File system standards of various OS is the same.

options.label: C
options.text: Aging is the solution of the starvation problem in the case of priority scheduling.

options.label: D
options.text: Critical section is a resource that cannot be accessed by multiple processes concurrently.

question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Made the two false statements explicitly selectable and qualified the aging claim.
assumptions: The question asks for false statements.
The priority scheme permits aging to overcome indefinite postponement.

reviews.hint: Separate creation, image replacement and termination; classify termination by its cause.
reviews.explanation: OS07 states that fork() creates a child in POSIX-style systems, returning zero in the child and its PID in the parent on success. exec replaces the current process image and does not itself create another process. exit and abort terminate execution normally and abnormally respectively. Creation therefore corresponds to fork among the literal listed calls.

evidence.quote: In POSIX-style systems fork() creates a child: zero is returned in the child and the child PID in the parent on success. The two have distinct address spaces, although resources may be shared through explicit mechanisms. exec replaces the current process image; it does not itself create another process.

Normal completion and a program-detected error exit are voluntary; an unrecoverable fault or being killed is involuntary. exit() terminates normally through the runtime; abort() requests abnormal termination.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: fork creates a child process rather than replacing or terminating the existing process image.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: exit terminates normally through the runtime rather than creating a new process.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: abort requests abnormal termination rather than allocating a new child execution instance.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: exec replaces the current process image; it does not itself create another process.

reviews.hint: Track available permits and blocked operations using the stated semaphore model.
reviews.explanation: OS12 explicitly says a semaphore can coordinate more than two processes, while classic Peterson’s algorithm is for two under its memory-model assumptions. OS11 explains counting semaphores as tracking several permits, fitting multiple resource instances. Compare-and-swap and test-and-set are atomic primitives rather than the named software coordination abstraction requested by the stem.

evidence.quote: A semaphore provides atomic wait/P/down and signal/V/up operations. Under the nonnegative-token model, wait consumes one available token or blocks when none is available; signal supplies a token and may wake a waiter. Implementations using negative internal counts encode waiters differently, so state the model. A binary semaphore represents one permit; a counting semaphore tracks several. A mutex normally has ownership rules that a general semaphore lacks.

Test-and-set and compare-and-swap combine checking/updating atomically; ordinary check-then-write does not. Peterson’s classic algorithm uses flags plus turn for two processes under its memory-model assumptions; a semaphore can coordinate more than two.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Counting semaphores track multiple permits and coordinate more than two participating processes.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Compare-and-swap is an atomic checking/updating primitive, rather than the requested software semaphore abstraction.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Classic Peterson’s algorithm solves the two-process case, not the stated more-than-two configuration.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Test-and-set is an atomic primitive; the software multiple-permit coordination mechanism here is a semaphore.

reviews.answer_text: All listed causes can terminate a process.
reviews.hint: Separate creation, image replacement and termination; classify termination by its cause.
reviews.explanation: OS07 distinguishes voluntary normal completion from involuntary faults or being killed. Each named cause is therefore a genuine termination cause, although the causes differ in who initiates them and whether completion is normal. The aggregate choice includes all three. Selecting only one named cause would omit other valid termination paths supported by the complete note.

evidence.quote: Normal completion and a program-detected error exit are voluntary; an unrecoverable fault or being killed is involuntary. exit() terminates normally through the runtime; abort() requests abnormal termination.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Being killed can terminate a process, but this alone omits normal completion and fatal faults.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Normal exit is valid, but it is only one of the three supported termination causes.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Being killed, normal exit and fatal error all provide legitimate process-termination causes.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A fatal error can terminate execution, but the other two named causes are also valid.

reviews.answer_text: All named conditions are necessary conditions.
reviews.hint: Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock.
reviews.explanation: OS22 lists mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no resource preemption and circular wait as necessary in the standard reusable-resource model. The three substantive choices name the first three, so all of the mentioned is the comprehensive option. Circular wait is also required despite being omitted from the list. Having these policies does not prove a particular current allocation is already deadlocked.

evidence.quote: Mutual exclusion allows at most one holder of a nonshareable resource. Hold-and-wait means retaining a resource while requesting another. No resource preemption means release must be voluntary. Circular wait forms a closed chain of such waits.
All four are necessary in the standard reusable-resource model.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Mutual exclusion is necessary, but selecting it alone omits the other two necessary conditions offered.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Each substantive option names a standard necessary deadlock condition; the aggregate includes all offered conditions.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Retaining resources while requesting more is hold-and-wait, one valid condition among the three offered.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: No forced removal is no-preemption, which is necessary but does not exclude the other valid conditions.

reviews.answer_text: Tree directory structure, in the usual general-purpose OS sense.
reviews.hint: Follow namespace structure and distinguish names, underlying files and mounted filesystems.
reviews.explanation: OS37 states that modern general-purpose systems commonly present hierarchical namespaces and defines a tree as allowing nested directories and absolute/relative paths. That directly supports the conventional tree-directory choice. This is a general-purpose namespace convention, not a measured claim about every OS ever built; links can add graph structure without replacing the hierarchy as the basic user-visible organization.

evidence.quote: A single-level directory requires unique names in one namespace. Two-level directories separate users. A tree allows nested directories and absolute/relative paths; links can create shared graphs. Modern general-purpose systems commonly present hierarchical namespaces, but a feature name alone does not prove that every system excludes simpler arrangements.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A single namespace without nested directories does not match the common hierarchical organization described.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Separating user directories alone is less general than the nested hierarchy specified for modern general-purpose systems.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Nested directories and paths form the tree/hierarchical organization the note identifies as commonly presented.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Links can add graph sharing, but acyclic sharing is not the basic common directory organization identified.

reviews.answer_text: All four are standard necessary deadlock conditions.
reviews.hint: Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock.
reviews.explanation: OS22 lists mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no-preemption and circular wait as the four necessary conditions in the standard reusable-resource model. Each substantive choice therefore names a valid deadlock condition, making all of these the comprehensive answer. The wording causes must not be read as saying one condition alone is sufficient; actual allocation/request dependencies still require inspection.

evidence.quote: Mutual exclusion allows at most one holder of a nonshareable resource. Hold-and-wait means retaining a resource while requesting another. No resource preemption means release must be voluntary. Circular wait forms a closed chain of such waits.
All four are necessary in the standard reusable-resource model. Their availability as general system policies does not prove a deadlock exists at this instant; inspect actual allocations/requests.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Mutual exclusion is one necessary condition, but the other three named conditions also belong to the standard set.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Hold-and-wait is necessary, but selecting it alone leaves out the other valid conditions.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Circular wait is part of the condition set, but it is not the sole valid listed condition.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: No-preemption is necessary in this model, alongside the other three substantive choices.

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: All four substantive choices are standard necessary conditions; together their names give the complete condition set.

reviews.answer_text: Each process is blocked waiting for an event or resource that only another blocked member of the set can provide
reviews.hint: Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock.
reviews.explanation: Deadlock requires blocked participants whose needed event or resource can be supplied only by another blocked participant in the same set. The closed dependency prevents any member from progressing without intervention. Terminated processes are no longer waiting, and attempts to kill one another do not establish a resource dependency. The revised blocking option states the necessary relationship rather than merely predicting permanent delay.

evidence.quote: A set is deadlocked when each member waits for an event/resource that only another blocked member can provide. Mere waiting for another holder is normal blocking; indefinite unfair delay can be starvation without a cycle of dependencies.

Normal completion and a program-detected error exit are voluntary; an unrecoverable fault or being killed is involuntary. exit() terminates normally through the runtime; abort() requests abnormal termination.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Termination ends execution and does not define a set of blocked dependent processes.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Attempts to kill other processes do not establish deadlocked resource waits.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This states the closed dependency among blocked members that defines deadlock.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The revised C explicitly gives the deadlock definition, so none is false.

question_revision.original_stem: A set of processes is deadlock if ____________

original_options.label: B
original_options.text: All processes are trying to kill each other

original_options.label: C
original_options.text: Each process is blocked and will remain so forever

question_revision.stem: In the standard reusable-resource model, a set of processes is deadlocked when ____________.

options.label: B
options.text: All processes are trying to kill each other

options.label: C
options.text: Each process is blocked waiting for an event or resource that only another blocked member of the set can provide

question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Added the missing closed resource/event dependency to the blocking option.
assumptions: Standard reusable-resource deadlock is intended.

reviews.hint: Apply the stated hole-selection or base-and-bound rule with its explicit convention.
reviews.explanation: OS28 defines worst-fit as selecting the largest hole, directly matching the stem. Best-fit chooses the smallest adequate hole, and first-fit stops at the first adequate one rather than comparing all sizes. The buddy label does not state this largest-hole rule in the provided note. No numeric trace is necessary because the selection criterion itself is explicit.

evidence.quote: First-fit selects the first adequate hole; next-fit continues from the previous search position; best-fit selects the smallest adequate hole; worst-fit selects the largest.

A buddy allocator manages power-of-two block sizes. It takes a smallest sufficient block, splitting larger blocks when necessary, and can merge a freed block with its free buddy. This is not the worst-fit rule of selecting the largest arbitrary hole.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Best-fit chooses the smallest adequate hole, which is the opposite size-selection criterion from the stem.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: First-fit selects the first adequate hole in search order, not necessarily the largest available hole.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Worst-fit is explicitly the policy that selects the largest available adequate hole.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The supplied largest-hole criterion is defined as worst-fit; the buddy label is not that rule.

reviews.hint: Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms.
reviews.explanation: OS34 defines plug-and-play as discovering and configuring compatible new hardware, with the qualification that a driver may still be required. That is exactly the printer scenario. The automatic wording excludes the two manual alternatives. Resource allocation may occur during configuration, but it is broader than the specific automatic detection/configuration feature requested by the question.

evidence.quote: Plug-and-play discovers/configures compatible new hardware but may still require a driver.
A driver converts OS requests into device-specific operations. Device independence and uniform naming hide brand-specific details; error handling reports/retries supported failures.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Automatically discovering and configuring the installed printer is precisely the plug-and-play behavior described.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The scenario explicitly says automatic detection/configuration rather than manual driver installation by the user.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Manual hardware management conflicts with the automatic configuration behavior specified in the scenario.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Resources may be assigned during setup, but the specific automatic discovery feature is plug-and-play.

reviews.hint: Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock.
reviews.explanation: OS22 directly defines no resource preemption as requiring voluntary release. The stem repeats that resources cannot be forcibly taken, so the match is exact. Hold-and-wait concerns retaining one resource while requesting another, mutual exclusion concerns exclusive possession, and circular wait concerns a closed dependency chain. None of those separately states the prohibition on forced withdrawal.

evidence.quote: Mutual exclusion allows at most one holder of a nonshareable resource. Hold-and-wait means retaining a resource while requesting another. No resource preemption means release must be voluntary. Circular wait forms a closed chain of such waits.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Prohibiting forced withdrawal and requiring voluntary release is exactly the no-preemption resource condition.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Hold-and-wait concerns retaining a resource while requesting another, not whether forced removal is permitted.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Mutual exclusion limits concurrent holders; it does not itself require voluntary release.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Circular wait describes a closed chain of dependencies rather than the resource-withdrawal rule.

reviews.hint: Separate creation, image replacement and termination; classify termination by its cause.
reviews.explanation: An externally imposed kill and an unrecoverable execution fault stop a process involuntarily. Normal completion is chosen by the program, and detecting an input error then exiting is also a voluntary program decision. The clarified meanings separate causes of termination instead of treating every use of the word terminate as one category. Thus the external-kill and fatal-fault choices are selected.

evidence.quote: Normal completion and a program-detected error exit are voluntary; an unrecoverable fault or being killed is involuntary. exit() terminates normally through the runtime; abort() requests abnormal termination.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Normal completion is a voluntary exit.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The defined external kill imposes termination and is involuntary.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: An unrecoverable execution fault imposes termination and is involuntary.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The program-detected error exit is a voluntary decision under the stated meaning.

question_revision.original_stem: Which one of the following exit is an involuntary action?
question_revision.stem: Which exits are involuntary? Here “Terminate exit” means an externally imposed kill, “Fatal exit” means an unrecoverable execution fault, and “Error exit” means the program chooses to exit after detecting bad input. Select all that apply.
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Defined the exit taxonomy and made all imposed exits selectable.
assumptions: Terminate exit denotes an external kill.
Fatal exit denotes an unrecoverable fault.
Error exit denotes an application-chosen response to bad input.

reviews.answer_text: Neither schedule is universally best; the choice trades detection overhead against delay
reviews.hint: Separate handling before allocation from actions taken after detection, and consider the cost of checking.
reviews.explanation: Checking after every request can discover a problem promptly but incurs repeated detection overhead. Periodic checking reduces check frequency while allowing a deadlock to persist until the next check. Which tradeoff is suitable depends on workload and acceptable detection delay. Without those criteria neither schedule is universally optimal, nor is there a basis for claiming they are always equally good.

evidence.quote: Checking on every request versus periodically trades overhead against detection delay; no universal best interval exists.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The two policies need not have equal overhead or detection delay.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Fixed intervals may suit some workloads, but no universal optimum follows.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Per-request checks can impose excessive overhead despite earlier detection.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This states the overhead-versus-delay tradeoff without asserting an unsupported universal optimum.

question_revision.original_stem: For an effective operating system, when should we check for deadlock?

original_options.label: A
original_options.text: Every time a resource request is made at fixed time intervals.

original_options.label: C
original_options.text: Every time a resource request is made.

question_revision.stem: An OS designer must choose between checking for deadlock after every resource request and checking periodically. No detection cost, request rate or acceptable delay is specified. Which conclusion about a universally best checking schedule is justified?

options.label: A
options.text: Both checking on every request and checking periodically are always equally optimal

options.label: B
options.text: Checking at fixed time intervals is always optimal

options.label: C
options.text: Checking on every resource request is always optimal

options.label: D
options.text: Neither schedule is universally best; the choice trades detection overhead against delay

question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Recast the overlapping schedules as explicit claims about universal optimality.
assumptions: Only the general overhead/delay tradeoff is supplied; no workload-specific optimum is implied.

reviews.hint: Identify whether data is in transit, retained for reuse or queued for a device.
reviews.explanation: Disk initialization and filesystem creation are identified as OS/tool work. Firmware starts the boot sequence before the kernel takes control, while a drive may use its own firmware to remap defective sectors. The question asks about that direct responsibility boundary, rather than broad coordination of every disk-related activity. Consequently disk initialization is the only matching choice, and the aggregate is too broad.

evidence.quote: Disk initialization/filesystem creation is OS/tool work, firmware begins boot, and drive firmware may remap bad sectors.
Firmware/bootloader stages execute before transferring control to a kernel loaded into RAM.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The specified bad-sector remapping is drive-firmware work, not the requested OS/tool operation.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The stage beginning boot is firmware work before kernel control.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Disk initialization/filesystem preparation is OS/tool work.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The other operations include firmware responsibilities, so all is too broad.

question_revision.original_stem: The operating system is responsible for?
question_revision.stem: Which listed operation is directly an OS/tool task? Here “bad-block recovery” specifically means autonomous drive-internal sector remapping, and “booting from disk” means the initial power-on stage before the kernel has been loaded.
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Specified direct OS/tool responsibility and separated the firmware stages.
assumptions: Bad-block recovery here refers to drive-firmware sector remapping.
Booting refers to the initial firmware stage, not the complete boot chain.

reviews.answer_text: A semaphore can enforce one-at-a-time access.
reviews.hint: Track available permits and blocked operations using the stated semaphore model.
reviews.explanation: OS11 describes a binary semaphore as one permit and gives wait(m); critical work; signal(m) with m initialized to 1. This prevents competing threads/processes from entering the protected resource operation simultaneously; it does not mean nobody can ever use the resource. A PCB stores process state, a scheduler selects jobs, and allocation layout does not enforce this resource-access rule.

evidence.quote: A semaphore provides atomic wait/P/down and signal/V/up operations. Under the nonnegative-token model, wait consumes one available token or blocks when none is available; signal supplies a token and may wake a waiter. Implementations using negative internal counts encode waiters differently, so state the model. A binary semaphore represents one permit; a counting semaphore tracks several. A mutex normally has ownership rules that a general semaphore lacks.

Initialize a mutex semaphore to 1. Each thread does wait(m); critical work; signal(m). For a buffer of N slots use empty=N, full=0 and mutex=1: producer waits empty then mutex, inserts, unlocks then signals full. Waiting for empty while already holding mutex can prevent the consumer from freeing a slot.
A saved PC identifies where execution resumes.
Long-term scheduling admits jobs; medium-term scheduling suspends/swaps them; short-term scheduling selects ready work.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A PCB records execution and resource state rather than supplying atomic mutual-exclusion operations.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A one-permit semaphore with atomic wait/signal can serialize entry to the protected resource operation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A job scheduler selects admitted or ready work; it does not by itself protect shared resource accesses.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Noncontiguous memory placement changes allocation layout rather than synchronizing access to one shared resource.

reviews.answer_text: Microsoft Office is an application suite.
reviews.hint: Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability.
reviews.explanation: OS40 explicitly identifies Microsoft Office as an application suite and discusses Windows, Linux and macOS as OS/kernel families. Office runs using OS services rather than providing the core resource-management platform. Thus Office is the exclusion in this list. The kernel-versus-distribution distinction for Linux does not turn it into an office application or invalidate the conventional OS-family contrast.

evidence.quote: Linux is a Unix-compatible kernel written from scratch by Linus Torvalds; a distribution combines it with userland, libraries and tools. Android’s base kernel layer is Linux; its framework and applications are higher layers. AOSP is open source, while a shipped device can include proprietary applications/services. Windows and macOS are both proprietary products, although macOS contains open-source components, so “which is not open source?” offering both is ambiguous. Microsoft Office is an application suite.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Windows is identified as the Microsoft operating-system family, so it is not the application-suite exclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Linux names a kernel used with distributions as operating systems, unlike the Office application suite.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: macOS is an operating-system product rather than a user application suite in this classification.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Microsoft Office is explicitly described as an application suite, not an operating system.

reviews.hint: Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task.
reviews.explanation: OS04 defines virtualization as presenting virtual machine environments and distinguishes it from virtual memory. OS27 describes swapping, OS30 paging and OS31 segmentation as memory-management mechanisms. Under the guest-machine sense used in this note, virtualization is therefore the option outside that list. The answer depends on that stated sense; the broader phrase memory virtualization would describe a different use of the word.

evidence.quote: Virtualization presents a virtual machine environment, often allowing guest operating systems on one host through a hypervisor. It differs from virtual memory, which translates a process’s addresses. Kernel, shell, API and VM are not interchangeable labels.
Swapping traditionally moves a whole process to backing store; paging moves individual pages.
Pages and physical frames have equal fixed size P. Divide virtual address v into page=floor(v/P) and offset=v mod P. The page table maps a page to a frame and protection/status flags.
Segmentation uses logical variable-length units such as code, stack and arrays.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Paging maps fixed-size virtual pages to physical frames and is explicitly a memory-management mechanism.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Segmentation maps variable-length logical regions and is explicitly a memory-management mechanism.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Swapping moves a process to backing store and is a memory-management operation described by the note.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: In the note’s guest-machine sense, virtualization presents virtual computers rather than naming these process-memory techniques.

reviews.answer_text: Binary Search Tree is a data structure.
reviews.hint: Separate class assignment, movement between queues and the rule for choosing work.
reviews.explanation: OS19 explicitly states that a binary search tree may implement a queue but is not itself a CPU selection policy. FCFS, Round Robin and SJF are actual scheduling algorithms described in OS15, OS18 and OS16. Consequently BST is the exclusion. Using a tree internally to maintain priorities would not change the selection policy into an algorithm called BST.

evidence.quote: A binary search tree is a data structure that might implement a queue; it is not itself a CPU selection policy.
FCFS runs ready bursts in arrival order and ordinarily does not preempt.
Non-preemptive SJF/SJN chooses the shortest next burst among currently ready jobs.
RR serves a ready queue cyclically for at most quantum q per turn.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: FCFS is a scheduling policy that runs ready bursts in their arrival order.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Round Robin is a scheduling policy assigning cyclic ready-queue turns bounded by a quantum.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: SJF is a scheduling policy selecting the shortest next burst among ready jobs.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: BST is a data structure that can support queue operations rather than a CPU scheduling policy.

reviews.answer_text: HTTP is an application communication protocol.
reviews.hint: Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata.
reviews.explanation: OS36 explicitly names FAT32, NTFS and ext4 as filesystem formats and contrasts HTTP as an application communication protocol. Filesystems organize stored file content and metadata; a communication protocol does not become a filesystem merely because it transfers file contents. Therefore HTTP is the single option outside the stated filesystem-format category.

evidence.quote: Sockets also support ordinary read/write, alongside socket/connect/send operations, so read is not uniquely “not a network call.” FAT32, NTFS and ext4 are filesystem formats; HTTP is an application communication protocol.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: FAT32 is explicitly identified as a filesystem format, making it a member of the requested category.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: NTFS is explicitly identified as a filesystem format, not a communication-protocol exclusion.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: ext4 is explicitly identified as a filesystem format in the complete study note.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: HTTP is an application communication protocol rather than a filesystem format for organizing stored files.

reviews.answer_text: Command-line interface (CLI); Graphical user interface (GUI); Natural language interface (NLI); Virtual reality interface (VRI)
reviews.hint: Distinguish identity checks, permission checks and the particular security property at issue.
reviews.explanation: The notes recognize command lines, graphical interfaces, speech or natural-language interaction, and virtual-reality interaction as possible interface forms. An OS need not implement all of them for each form to count as a possible interface. Because the clarified question asks about capability in general rather than a particular product’s installed features, all four listed forms satisfy it.

evidence.quote: CLI, GUI, speech/natural language and VR are possible interfaces, not a closed list excluding the last two.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A CLI accepts text commands as a user interface.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A GUI provides graphical controls for user interaction.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Natural-language or speech interaction is a possible interface form.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: VR interaction is also a possible interface form.

question_revision.original_stem:
Which of the following is not a type of user interface used in operating
systems?
question_revision.stem: Which listed forms can serve as user interfaces to an operating system? Treat possible interface forms generally, rather than features of a particular product. Select all that apply.
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Asked for all possible interface forms instead of an unsupported exclusion.
assumptions: Possible interface forms are considered independently of any one OS product.

reviews.hint: Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting.
reviews.explanation: OS03 defines the kernel through core resource management, protection and system-call handling, while explicitly calling browsers applications. Scheduling, memory management and filesystem service are core resource-management functions in the textbook kernel sense. Some systems move services outside a kernel, but a web browser remains the clear application-level exclusion from the listed ordinary kernel responsibilities.

evidence.quote: The kernel implements core resource management, protection and system-call handling. A shell reads/interprets user commands; a GUI is another interface. Browsers, office tools and editors are applications.
An OS allocates CPU time, memory, storage, devices and communication resources, and provides services to programs.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Process scheduling is a core resource-management function in the textbook kernel model used here.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Memory management is a core resource-management function rather than the listed user application.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Filesystem service belongs to ordinary OS resource management in this textbook kernel-level comparison.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The note explicitly identifies browsers as applications rather than components implementing the kernel’s core role.

reviews.answer_text: Video editing is an application operation.
reviews.hint: Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task.
reviews.explanation: OS04 lists process control, file/device management, information retrieval and communication as service categories. It explicitly distinguishes video editing as an application operation. Network communication falls within communication services, so it is not excluded merely because it uses sockets rather than local files. The category outside generic system calls is video editing.

evidence.quote: Process control, file/device management, information retrieval and communication are service categories. Video editing and a database-specific write_database() are application operations, not standard generic syscall categories/names.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Process control is explicitly included among protected operating-system service categories.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: File management is explicitly included among operating-system services requested through system calls.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Network communication falls within the communication service category rather than being excluded from system calls.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Video editing is an application-level operation, not a standard generic system-call service category.

reviews.hint: Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability.
reviews.explanation: Windows and macOS are proprietary products. The existence of open-source components within macOS does not make the complete product open source. Linux is treated here as the open-source kernel, and Android is explicitly restricted to AOSP, excluding proprietary applications or services bundled by device vendors. With that component-versus-product scope fixed, both macOS and Windows belong in the selected set.

evidence.quote: Linux is a Unix-compatible kernel written from scratch by Linus Torvalds; a distribution combines it with userland, libraries and tools. Android’s base kernel layer is Linux; its framework and applications are higher layers. AOSP is open source, while a shipped device can include proprietary applications/services. Windows and macOS are both proprietary products, although macOS contains open-source components, so “which is not open source?” offering both is ambiguous. Microsoft Office is an application suite.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Linux is the open-source kernel under the stated scope.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: AOSP is open source; vendor additions are explicitly excluded.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: macOS is a proprietary product even though some components are open source.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Windows is a proprietary OS product.

question_revision.original_stem: Which of the following operating systems is not open source?
question_revision.stem: Which listed systems are proprietary OS products rather than open-source systems as a whole? Interpret Linux as the open-source kernel and Android as AOSP without vendor additions. Select all that apply.
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Made both proprietary products selectable and fixed the Android component scope.
assumptions: Android means AOSP without proprietary vendor additions.
macOS and Windows mean the complete OS products.

reviews.answer_text: Load the OS kernel into memory.
reviews.hint: Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting.
reviews.explanation: OS03 places firmware/bootloader stages before transfer of control to a kernel loaded into RAM. This identifies loading the kernel as the bootloader purpose among the alternatives. Resource management is subsequently a kernel role, application management is a running-system function, and user interfaces are provided by shells/GUI components rather than defining the bootloader’s purpose.

evidence.quote: Firmware/bootloader stages execute before transferring control to a kernel loaded into RAM.

The kernel implements core resource management, protection and system-call handling. A shell reads/interprets user commands; a GUI is another interface. Browsers, office tools and editors are applications.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The bootloader prepares the kernel in memory and transfers control to it during the boot sequence.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Core hardware-resource management is the kernel’s role after the bootloader hands over control.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Managing running applications belongs to the operating system’s runtime services rather than defining the bootloader.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Shells and GUIs provide user interfaces; that is not the bootloader’s principal role here.

reviews.hint: Compute remaining needs and simulate feasible completions before deciding whether an allocation is safe.
reviews.explanation: Banker’s algorithm checks whether tentative allocations leave a safe completion sequence and is an avoidance method. Wait-for and resource-allocation graphs represent dependencies used in deadlock reasoning. A binary search tree is a general data structure and does not, by its name alone, specify deadlock handling. The clarified broader category distinguishes the unrelated item without misclassifying avoidance or detection as strict prevention.

evidence.quote: Avoidance allows requests only if the resulting state remains safe. Banker requires maximum claims. Compute Need=Max−Allocation.

In a resource-allocation graph, P→R is a request and an instance R→P is an assignment. Follow these directions to form waits. No cycle implies no deadlock; with one instance of every resource type, a cycle implies deadlock. With multiple instances a cycle alone is insufficient: another instance may permit completion. A wait-for graph replaces single-instance resource nodes with P→Q when P waits for Q.
A binary search tree is a data structure that might implement a queue; it is not itself a CPU selection policy.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Banker is a deadlock-avoidance method, so it belongs to the stated handling category.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A wait-for graph directly represents process dependencies for deadlock analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A resource-allocation graph represents resource requests and assignments for deadlock reasoning.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A binary search tree is a general search structure rather than a deadlock-specific method.

question_revision.original_stem:
14.Which of the following is not a type of deadlock prevention algorithm used
in operating systems?
question_revision.stem: Which listed item is a general data structure rather than a deadlock-specific avoidance method or dependency-graph analysis?
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Replaced strict prevention with deadlock-specific handling and graph analysis.
assumptions: The category includes avoidance and dependency analysis rather than only condition-breaking prevention.

reviews.hint: Track available permits and blocked operations using the stated semaphore model.
reviews.explanation: OS10 describes monitors as protected operations with condition synchronization, and OS11 explains mutex/semaphore exclusion mechanisms. These coordinate concurrent execution. A keyboard is an input device rather than such a coordination abstraction. Interrupts generated by hardware may participate in event handling, but that does not make the keyboard itself a mutex, semaphore or monitor mechanism.

evidence.quote: A semaphore provides atomic wait/P/down and signal/V/up operations. Under the nonnegative-token model, wait consumes one available token or blocks when none is available; signal supplies a token and may wake a waiter. Implementations using negative internal counts encode waiters differently, so state the model. A binary semaphore represents one permit; a counting semaphore tracks several. A mutex normally has ownership rules that a general semaphore lacks.
A barrier waits until a defined set of participants reaches a point; a monitor encapsulates protected operations with condition synchronization.
Input/output/storage/NIC devices are OS-managed hardware; user accounts are identities.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A mutex provides owned mutual exclusion and is a synchronization mechanism in the note.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A semaphore coordinates participants through atomic wait and signal operations, so it is a synchronization mechanism.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A monitor combines protected operations and condition synchronization, making it a genuine synchronization abstraction.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A keyboard is a physical input device rather than a process/thread synchronization abstraction.

reviews.hint: Identify how data moves, which participant waits and what event allows the operation to continue.
reviews.explanation: Pipes provide streams, shared memory provides a common region, and message queues preserve messages. These are primitive IPC mechanisms in the stated classification. HTTP is an application protocol that can use an underlying communication mechanism such as sockets. It can certainly carry interprocess communication, but it is the only listed application-layer protocol rather than one of the primitive mechanisms requested here.

evidence.quote: Shared memory lets processes access a common region and requires synchronization for conflicting updates. Message passing exchanges data through send/receive operations. Pipes provide streams; message queues preserve messages; sockets connect endpoints; RPC requests a remote operation. HTTP is an application protocol over a communication mechanism and can carry interprocess communication, so it is not universally “not IPC.”

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Pipes are primitive stream-based IPC mechanisms.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Shared memory is a primitive common-region IPC mechanism.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Message queues are primitive message-preserving IPC mechanisms.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: HTTP requests use an application-layer protocol over an underlying mechanism.

question_revision.original_stem:
Which of the following is not a type of interprocess communication
mechanism used in operating systems?
question_revision.stem: Which item is an application-layer protocol rather than a primitive OS IPC mechanism such as a stream, shared region or message queue?
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Restricted the classification to primitive OS IPC mechanisms versus application protocols.
assumptions: The question classifies abstraction layers, not whether data can pass between processes.

reviews.answer_text: Infinite is not a scheduling-policy category.
reviews.hint: Check whether the running burst can be interrupted before completion or blocking.
reviews.explanation: OS14 distinguishes preemptive and non-preemptive scheduling and explains cooperative scheduling as relying on voluntary release. OS19 explicitly rejects Infinite as a standard scheduling-policy category. Thus the first three labels describe genuine scheduling approaches, whereas infinite does not identify a selection or preemption rule. It should not be confused with a possible unbounded waiting-time outcome.

evidence.quote: Non-preemptive scheduling keeps a running CPU burst until completion, blocking or voluntary yielding. Preemptive scheduling can return running work to ready, usually after a timer quantum or a more urgent arrival. FCFS and non-preemptive SJF are non-preemptive; RR and SRTF are preemptive. Priority can be either, so its name alone cannot decide. Cooperative describes relying on voluntary release.
“Infinite” is not a standard scheduling-policy category.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Preemptive scheduling can interrupt running work and return it to the ready state.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Non-preemptive scheduling retains a running burst until completion, blocking or voluntary release.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Cooperative scheduling is the recognized approach relying on voluntary release of execution.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Infinite names no scheduling selection or preemption policy in the provided note.

reviews.hint: Identify whether data is in transit, retained for reuse or queued for a device.
reviews.explanation: OS35 says a system monitor reports CPU, memory, storage and network usage and measures rather than creating more resources. This matches providing information about performance and usage. User-account administration, hardware allocation and application management are broader OS/administration functions, not the monitor’s defining reporting role. Observing a resource is distinct from allocating or increasing it.

evidence.quote: A system monitor reports CPU, memory, storage and network usage; it measures rather than directly creating more resources.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Account management is an administration function, not the monitor’s specified performance-reporting purpose.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The monitor measures hardware usage rather than serving as the general resource-allocation manager.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Application management is broader than the monitor’s role of reporting system performance and consumption.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Reporting system performance and resource usage directly matches the monitor definition in the note.

reviews.answer_text: write_database() is not a standard generic file-management system call.
reviews.hint: Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata.
reviews.explanation: OS36 identifies open, close and read as ordinary file operations, and OS04 explicitly distinguishes database-specific write_database() as an application operation rather than a standard generic syscall name. A database operation may internally use actual file syscalls, but that composition does not make its application-specific name a generic kernel file-management call.

evidence.quote: A file has content and metadata such as name, size, owner, permissions and timestamps. open obtains an open-file reference, read/write transfer bytes, seek changes an offset, close releases a reference, truncate changes size and unlink removes a name.

Process control, file/device management, information retrieval and communication are service categories. Video editing and a database-specific write_database() are application operations, not standard generic syscall categories/names.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: open obtains an open-file reference and is a standard file-management operation described by the note.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: close releases an open-file reference and is a standard file-management operation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: read transfers bytes from an open resource and is a standard generic file operation.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: write_database is an application-specific database operation rather than a standard generic file-management syscall.

reviews.hint: Identify conflicting shared accesses and the safety or progress property required.
reviews.explanation: Locks coordinate entry to protected state, barriers wait for participants to reach a common point, and monitors encapsulate protected operations with conditions. Interrupts notify the CPU of events and may help coordinate work, but belong to a different abstraction level. The clarified classification therefore selects interrupts without denying that interrupts can participate in synchronization or completion notification.

evidence.quote: Keep critical regions small and ensure every conflicting access uses the same protection. A barrier waits until a defined set of participants reaches a point; a monitor encapsulates protected operations with condition synchronization.
A mutex normally has ownership rules that a general semaphore lacks.
Polling checks readiness repeatedly; interrupts request CPU attention; DMA transfers blocks after setup without CPU work for every byte.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A lock is a high-level mutual-exclusion abstraction.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A barrier is a participant rendezvous abstraction.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A monitor encapsulates protected operations and condition synchronization.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: An interrupt is a CPU event-notification mechanism, the different abstraction level requested.

question_revision.original_stem:
Which of the following is not a type of process synchronization mechanism
used in operating systems?
question_revision.stem: Which item is a hardware/CPU event-notification mechanism rather than a high-level lock, participant rendezvous, or protected-operation abstraction?
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Specify the abstraction level of the compared mechanisms.
assumptions: Classification is by event mechanism versus high-level synchronization abstraction.

reviews.answer_text: A virtualized environment can run guest operating systems on one physical host.
reviews.hint: Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task.
reviews.explanation: OS04 defines virtualization as presenting a virtual machine environment, often allowing guest operating systems on one host through a hypervisor. That is exactly the complete description in D. Account, hardware and application management may occur within host or guest systems, but those broad administrative roles do not define why a virtual machine is provided.

evidence.quote: Virtualization presents a virtual machine environment, often allowing guest operating systems on one host through a hypervisor. It differs from virtual memory, which translates a process’s addresses. Kernel, shell, API and VM are not interchangeable labels.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: User-account management is not the defining purpose of presenting a virtual machine environment.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Hardware is mediated, but general hardware management alone omits the guest-machine environment requested.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Application management does not define a virtual machine or distinguish it from an ordinary running OS.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Providing guest-machine environments on one physical host directly matches the note’s virtualization definition.

reviews.hint: Identify how data moves, which participant waits and what event allows the operation to continue.
reviews.explanation: Message passing transfers messages, shared memory carries data through a common region, and RPC requests an operation in another process or machine. File locking instead coordinates who may access a file or region. Locks can therefore be part of IPC synchronization while not being a payload-transfer mechanism themselves. The narrower wording makes file locking the unique match without denying its coordination role.

evidence.quote: Shared memory lets processes access a common region and requires synchronization for conflicting updates. Message passing exchanges data through send/receive operations. Pipes provide streams; message queues preserve messages; sockets connect endpoints; RPC requests a remote operation.
File locks coordinate access rather than transfer arbitrary payloads, though locking is synchronization within IPC.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Message passing transfers data using send/receive operations.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Shared memory carries data in a common accessible region.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: RPC communicates a request to perform another process’s operation.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: File locking coordinates access rather than carrying arbitrary payloads itself.

question_revision.original_stem:
Which of the following is not a type of process communication mechanism
used in operating systems?
question_revision.stem: Which item coordinates access but does not itself transfer arbitrary data payloads or request an operation in another process?
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Restricted the distinction to payload/operation transfer versus access coordination.
assumptions: Indirect signaling through lock state is not treated as arbitrary payload transfer.

reviews.answer_text:
A process can have multiple tasks, while a task can only belong to one
process
reviews.hint: Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping.
reviews.explanation: With task explicitly defined to mean thread, a process may contain several tasks while each task belongs to one process at a time. The tasks share the process address space but have their own execution context. This ownership relationship does not follow from the word task universally; it follows from the definition supplied here. Execution-versus-scheduling slogans do not state that relationship.

evidence.quote: A thread has its own PC, registers and stack. Threads in a process share code, address space and usually open-file resources. A process can contain many threads; a thread belongs to one process at a time. Threads are not a group of processes and need not execute sequentially. Independent processes can exist; cooperating ones communicate/share data.
Task is OS-specific terminology: it may mean process, thread or schedulable entity.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A thread/task is not identical to its containing process under this definition.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The execution-versus-scheduling description does not express the defined ownership relationship.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A process can contain multiple threads/tasks, each belonging to one process at a time.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The reversed execution/scheduling labels do not describe thread ownership.

question_revision.original_stem: What is the difference between a process and a task in an operating system?

original_options.label: A
original_options.text: There is no difference between a process and a task

original_options.label: B
original_options.text: A process is a unit of execution, while a task is a unit of scheduling

original_options.label: C
original_options.text:
A process can have multiple tasks, while a task can only belong to one
process

original_options.label: D
original_options.text: A task is a unit of execution, while a process is a unit of scheduling

question_revision.stem: In this question only, “task” means a thread within a process. Which statement describes the process–task ownership relationship?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no difference between a process and a task

options.label: B
options.text: A process is a unit of execution, while a task is a unit of scheduling

options.label: C
options.text:
A process can have multiple tasks, while a task can only belong to one
process

options.label: D
options.text: A task is a unit of execution, while a process is a unit of scheduling

question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Defined task as thread and asked specifically for the ownership relationship.
assumptions: Task means thread only for this practice item.

reviews.answer_text: Binary-Fit is not one of the standard fit-policy names.
reviews.hint: Apply the stated hole-selection or base-and-bound rule with its explicit convention.
reviews.explanation: OS28 defines first-fit, next-fit, best-fit and worst-fit, then explicitly says binary-fit is not one of these standard names. First-fit, best-fit and next-fit therefore belong to the allocation-policy category used by the question. Binary-fit is the supported exclusion; it should not be invented as a synonym for another algorithm merely because the word binary is familiar.

evidence.quote: First-fit selects the first adequate hole; next-fit continues from the previous search position; best-fit selects the smallest adequate hole; worst-fit selects the largest. No policy universally optimizes both search time and future storage utilization. Binary-fit is not one of these standard names.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: First-fit selects the first adequate hole and is an explicitly defined memory-allocation policy.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Best-fit chooses the smallest adequate hole and is an explicitly defined memory-allocation policy.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Next-fit resumes search from the previous position and is an explicitly defined allocation policy.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The note explicitly excludes binary-fit from the standard memory-allocation fit-policy names.

reviews.answer_text: Provide the interface through which applications request system calls.
reviews.hint: Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task.
reviews.explanation: OS04 defines a system call as requesting a protected kernel service and distinguishes an API/library wrapper from the direct boundary. Option D describes the interface that applications use to make those requests. Account, hardware and application management can be services reached through it; they are not the general purpose of the interface itself.

evidence.quote: A system call requests a protected kernel service, such as creating a process, reading a file or opening a socket. A user-facing API/library may wrap that request; not every library function enters the kernel. Therefore a stem asking merely for the interface to OS services must distinguish the application API from the direct user/kernel boundary.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Account operations may be exposed as services, but account management does not define the interface itself.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Hardware operations may be requested through services; general hardware management is not the interface definition.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Application management is a possible service use rather than the purpose of the syscall interface.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The interface supplies the application-to-system-call request path for protected kernel services.

reviews.hint: Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata.
reviews.explanation: Sockets can support the ordinary read/write interface as well as specialized socket operations. A read therefore need not be confined to disk files: it can receive bytes from a socket descriptor. socket creates an endpoint, connect establishes a connection, and send transmits data. Only read matches both the generic file-input role and the ability to receive socket data in this model.

evidence.quote: Sockets also support ordinary read/write, alongside socket/connect/send operations, so read is not uniquely “not a network call.” FAT32, NTFS and ext4 are filesystem formats; HTTP is an application communication protocol.

In the descriptor-based socket API, socket() creates a communication endpoint and returns its descriptor. connect() associates the socket with the requested peer address; send() transmits data to another socket. Receiving through read() uses the ordinary descriptor-input interface described in the file-services lesson.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: socket creates a communication endpoint rather than reading bytes from it.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: connect establishes a connection rather than receiving its data.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: read is generic descriptor input and can receive bytes from a socket.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: send transmits data rather than performing the requested input operation.

question_revision.original_stem:
Which of the following is not a type of system call used in network
communication?
question_revision.stem: Which listed operation can receive bytes from a socket while also serving as a generic file-input operation in the descriptor model?
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Asked about the generic input operation shared by files and sockets.
assumptions: The descriptor-based socket model supporting ordinary read/write is intended.

reviews.answer_text: A process-local reference to an open file or communication endpoint.
reviews.hint: Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata.
reviews.explanation: OS36 defines a file descriptor as a process-local integer handle and separately places offset and access mode in associated open-file state. It also describes sockets supporting ordinary descriptor I/O. The descriptor therefore refers to an open resource or endpoint; it is not an account manager, hardware manager or application manager. D is the specific role matching that definition.

evidence.quote: A file has content and metadata such as name, size, owner, permissions and timestamps. open obtains an open-file reference, read/write transfer bytes, seek changes an offset, close releases a reference, truncate changes size and unlink removes a name. A file descriptor is a process-local integer handle; the associated open-file state contains the current offset and access mode.

Sockets also support ordinary read/write, alongside socket/connect/send operations, so read is not uniquely “not a network call.” FAT32, NTFS and ext4 are filesystem formats; HTTP is an application communication protocol.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A descriptor identifies an open resource within a process, rather than managing user accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A descriptor is a handle used to access a resource, not a general hardware-management component.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Descriptors support resource I/O and do not manage application lifecycles or software installations.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: An open-file or socket reference is the resource-handle purpose of a file descriptor.

reviews.answer_text: lack of paper in printer; connection failure in the network
reviews.hint: Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms.
reviews.explanation: OS I/O services can report or respond to a printer running out of paper and to a network connection failure. Complete unannounced loss of power without backup prevents the processor from continuing to run the OS, so software alone cannot handle it during continued execution. The aggregate option includes that unsupported case. Under the explicit power assumptions, the printer and network choices are selected.

evidence.quote: Printer-paper and network errors can be handled/reported, but continued operation during total power loss requires hardware support, not OS software alone.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The OS can report or handle an out-of-paper printer condition while running.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The OS can report or handle a network connection failure while running.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Complete unannounced power loss without backup prevents continued software execution.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: All includes the excluded total-power-loss case and is therefore incorrect.

question_revision.original_stem: Which one of the following errors will be handle by the operating system?
question_revision.stem: Which failures can OS software report or handle while it continues executing on powered hardware? C means complete power loss with no backup supply or advance notification. Select all that apply.
question_revision.note: Clarified practice version: Specified continued powered execution and selected all supported error examples.
assumptions: Handling includes reporting supported device/network errors.
Power failure means total unannounced loss without backup hardware.

reviews.hint: Compare the stated historical clues and distinguish origin, characteristic era and technical capability.
reviews.explanation: Dennis Ritchie is credited alongside Ken Thompson in Bell Labs’ account of UNIX’s creation. The original question’s undefined first-widely-used claim is replaced by this specific attribution, preserving its OS-history focus and original choices. OS40 supplies related historical cautions; the co-creator fact comes from the supplementary Bell Labs source, not from an added master-note claim. The other listed people are not that co-creator.

evidence.quote: UNIX development began at Bell Labs in 1969, led by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie with other collaborators. Ritchie is therefore a co-creator, not the sole inventor of the first operating system.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Babbage is not the UNIX co-creator alongside Thompson identified by Bell Labs.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Turing is not the UNIX co-creator alongside Thompson identified by Bell Labs.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Berners-Lee is not the UNIX co-creator alongside Thompson identified by Bell Labs.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Dennis Ritchie is the Bell Labs co-creator associated with Ken Thompson.

No additional market-history claim is needed to resolve the listed alternatives.

reviews.hint: Compare the stated historical clues and distinguish origin, characteristic era and technical capability.
reviews.explanation: UNIX began at Bell Labs in 1969. Ritchie and Thompson’s primary paper describes the later system as multiuser and interactive, with asynchronous processes. These historical identifying facts come from the supplementary sources. OS40 supplies the related caution that UNIX was not the first system ever to multitask. The revised question preserves the history and multitasking focus while dropping that false priority claim.

evidence.quote: UNIX development began at Bell Labs in 1969, led by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie with other collaborators. Ritchie is therefore a co-creator, not the sole inventor of the first operating system.

The later UNIX time-sharing system described by Ritchie and Thompson is multiuser and interactive and supports asynchronous processes. Its later versions incorporated multiprogramming. This history does not make UNIX the first system ever to multitask.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: MS-DOS is not the Bell Labs system originating in 1969.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: macOS is not the original Bell Labs system identified by that history.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Windows is not the Bell Labs system described by Ritchie and Thompson.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: UNIX matches the Bell Labs origin and the later multiuser time-sharing description.

question_revision.original_stem: Which operating system was the first to introduce multitasking, allowing multiple programs to run simultaneously?

Windows is the Microsoft family commonly described as succeeding the MS-DOS desktop era; Solaris originated at Sun.

choices.label: D

reviews.hint: Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability.
reviews.explanation: OS40 directly states that Solaris originated at Sun. That developer clue resolves the choices even though the note does not quantify Solaris’s reliability or scalability relative to other systems. The answer relies on the explicit origin, not on assuming those broad positive attributes uniquely distinguish one OS. Linux and Windows have separately identified developer lineages in the same section.

evidence.quote: Windows is the Microsoft family commonly described as succeeding the MS-DOS desktop era; Solaris originated at Sun.

choices.label: A

reviews.hint: Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability.
reviews.explanation: Android uses Linux at its base kernel layer, with framework and application layers above it. Its open-source base is AOSP, although shipped devices may contain proprietary services or applications. Those architectural facts identify Android without needing an unspecified population or a dated market-share claim. The other listed mobile systems are not the platform identified by this particular combination of Linux and AOSP.

evidence.quote: Android’s base kernel layer is Linux; its framework and applications are higher layers. AOSP is open source, while a shipped device can include proprietary applications/services.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: iOS is not the platform identified by the Linux/AOSP combination.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
